detail: You get someone who can make the abstract concrete. Complex problems, unclear briefs, tangled systems — I translate them into something a team can actually act on. That started with a degree in illustration at Falmouth and has never stopped scaling.

detail: Your team ships better work when nothing is hidden. I build cultures where showing early, inviting critique, and working in the open is just how things are done — not a value on a wall. Learned this properly at NixonMcInnes, practised it ever since.

detail: You get a design leader who engineers actually want in the room. I've been embedded in delivery teams since before cross-functional was a job description — which means I understand constraints, speak the language, and don't throw specs over a wall.

detail: You get someone who knows how large organisations actually move — and how to move them. Simplicity inside a complex institution requires patience, political fluency, the courage to cut, and a narrative that brings stakeholders with you. Five years at Lloyds Banking Group taught me all of that.

detail: You get someone who won't let the business railroad the user — or the other way around. I hold the tension between commercial pressure and real user need, and I don't let either side win too easily. That skill was forged at 4G Capital in East Africa, where the stakes were real and the easy answer was rarely the right one.

detail: You get someone who can change a large institution without being consumed by it. At JPMorgan Chase I apply everything above at global scale — pushing for unconventional thinking in a place that doesn't naturally reward it, and making changes that actually stick. Twenty years of an unusual career, finally in the right context.
